subject: general
question: According to Article 170, the number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State should not be more than _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**500**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 170 of the Indian Constitution pertains to the composition of the Legislative Assemblies in Indian states.
 
• According to this article, the number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State should not exceed 500.
 
• The Legislative Assembly is the lower house of the state legislature, also known as the Vidhan Sabha.
 
• This limit ensures a manageable size for the effective functioning of the legislative body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 170:**

 
 
• This article deals with the composition of the Legislative Assemblies in Indian states.
 
• It specifies the maximum and minimum number of members in the Legislative Assembly.
 
• Each state is divided into territorial constituencies in such manner that the ratio between the population of each constituency and the number of seats allotted to it is, so far as practicable, the same throughout the state.
 
• The total number of seats in the assembly of each state shall be determined by the population of the state.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha):**
 
 
• The Legislative Assembly is the lower house of the state legislature in India.
 
• Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) are elected directly by the people from single-member constituencies.
 
• The term of the Legislative Assembly is five years unless dissolved sooner.
 
• The size of the Legislative Assembly varies from state to state, depending on the population.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad):**
 
 
• Some states also have a Legislative Council, which is the upper house of the state legislature.
 
• Members of the Legislative Council (MLCs) are elected by a combination of direct and indirect elections.
 
• Not all states have a Legislative Council; it exists only in certain states as per the provisions of the Constitution.
 
• The Council acts as a revising chamber, providing a second opinion on bills passed by the Legislative Assembly.
 
 
 
• **Delimitation:**
 
 
• Delimitation refers to the act of redrawing the boundaries of electoral constituencies to reflect changes in population.
 
• This process ensures that each constituency has roughly the same number of inhabitants, maintaining fair representation.
 
• The Delimitation Commission is appointed by the President of India and works in collaboration with the Election Commission.
 
• The most recent delimitation exercise was conducted based on the 2001 Census data.
